old: An induction gathers scattered attention until quieter material becomes easier to hear. You don’t have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. When you’re sober, distracted, analytical, or guarded, an actual induction may help. When meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, or another intense opening has already made you trancey, begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth.
new: Do you need an induction? It may help to induce trance if you are sober, distracted, analytical, or otherwise not very trancey, as it is helpful to bring together your attention and make you more receptive to the quieter materials. You do not have to induce trance by having someone take over your will, making you fall asleep to play, or otherwise make you do something you don’t want to do. If you are already trancey from meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, etc., you can probably skip the induction and go straight to orientation and containment.

old: Aim for the amount of trance that suits the practice: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.
new: How much trance is enough? Enough trance for the practice to feel focused and warm, receptive and embodied, and for you to be able to stop the practice when you need to. Deeper trance may be useful, but it is not necessary.

old: “I do not need to hate this. I do not need to merge with this. I do not need to obey this. I do not need to defeat this from fear. I return to loving awareness.”
new: So the next time the enemy enters the room, simply say to it, “I see that there is no reason to hate or revile what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to merge with or become what I am experiencing. I see that there is no need to obey the voice in my head or in another. I see that there is no need to defeat what I am experiencing. I choose instead to return my attention to my loving awareness.”

old: Preview the sequence, choose one purpose, and decide whether you want to begin. Each family can be light, eyes-open, or replaced by no-trance contact. Notice the actual response—including no change—and let it determine the next move. Move, imagine, change the sensory channel, remain still, or stop. Use the complete waking return after every induction.
new: Practise: Preview, choose a purpose, decide to start. All ‘families’ can be light, eyes open or with no trance contact replacement. Monitor what happens (even if nothing seems to change) and decide on next action: move on, imagine, change sensory channel, remain still, stop the sequence etc. Always do a complete waking return from induction.

old: If vivid images don’t come, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial sense, touch, movement, or simple knowing. The mind doesn’t owe anybody a movie.
new: NB If you cannot ‘see’ any images vividly, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial relations, touch, movement, knowing etc.

old: Feel the support beneath you and the position of one hand or foot. Press gently, stretch slightly, and release—or imagine it. Notice ease, tension, warmth, breath, or no change. Repeat with no more than three areas, letting “release” guide the sequence. Which area or inner voice wants attention? What support is needed? Restore ordinary movement and return.
new: Focus on a feeling of support (and perhaps the position of one hand or foot). Either actually or in imagination stretch slightly and/or press into the support and then release. Notice any difference in feeling (even if nothing seems to change). Repeat this with no more than 3 areas of the body. Use the notion of ‘release’ to guide you through the sequence. Ask yourself where in your body (and/or voice) you need to stretch or release and what you need by way of support to do this. Then bring back normal movement and return.

old: Awareness verbs point attention without yelling at it: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider.
new: Try some of the other ‘awareness’ verbs: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider

old: Nominalizations turn processes into nouns: healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest. Their vagueness can sometimes help because the subconscious supplies its own concrete meaning.
new: Healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest, and other words like that are quite vague. And sometimes that vagueness is helpful because it lets the subconscious mind fill in the specifics in the most helpful way.

old: “A little more safety can arrive in whatever way the body understands.”
new: Why don't YOU let yourself become a bit safer now, in whatever way is most appropriate for YOUR body?

old: “What does one side want?” “What does the other side fear?” “What need sits under both?” “What third option honors both without letting either run the whole life?”
new: The Sacred Decision (What does one side want? What is the other side afraid of? What is the need of each side? What is a 3rd option that meets each sides needs while not letting one side completely dominate?)

new: Deny legitimate signals

new: Remove fear (only re-prioritize it to a more useful level)

new: Recover “memories”

new: Manipulate people (this includes myself)

new: Convince myself intuitions are true (that’s more carefully attending to the non-rational data stream)

new: Remove legitimate signals (pain, hunger, etc) or medical symptoms
